title: Published: how warming raises invertebrates’ energy demands
body:
Our paper, **Invertebrates' metabolic responses to climate warming scenarios in the Adriatic Sea**, is out in _Ecological Indicators_.

We measured the standard metabolic rate (the energy an animal needs at rest) of nine invertebrate species collected from the southern to the northern Adriatic, at two temperatures, then projected how it changes by 2100 under IPCC climate scenarios.

• Metabolic rate rose less steeply with body size and temperature than theory predicts.
• Even so, warming raises energy demands across the Adriatic: by 7.8% on average under the optimistic scenario (RCP2.6) and 27.3% under the severe one (RCP8.5).
• The northern basin, especially the Gulf of Trieste, is likely to be hit hardest.
